items.q: Grandma ______ the sticky rice for Tết right now, so the kitchen is full of steam.
items.vi: Bà đang đồ xôi cho Tết ngay lúc này nên bếp đầy hơi nước.
items.explanation: Right now points to an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is steaming is needed.

items.q: Vegetables are cheap at the village market; a whole basket of tomatoes only ______ 20,000 dong.
items.vi: Rau ở chợ làng rất rẻ; cả một rổ cà chua chỉ có giá 20.000 đồng.
items.explanation: A thing costs an amount of money; people pay or spend money, and a seller charges a price.

items.q: Lan: The recipe says 200 grams of sugar, but you used 210. / Nam: Let's not ______ — ten grams won't change the taste.
items.vi: Lan: Công thức ghi 200 gam đường mà cậu cho 210. / Nam: Đừng bắt bẻ từng li từng tí — mười gam chẳng làm đổi vị đâu.
items.explanation: To split hairs is to argue about tiny, unimportant differences. Cut corners means do something cheaply or carelessly, pull strings means use influence, and beat around the bush means avoid the main point.

items.q: Could you ______ the table before the guests arrive for the New Year dinner?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn trước khi khách đến dự bữa tối năm mới được không?
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is lay (or set) the table, meaning put out the plates and cutlery; make, put and do do not collocate with the table in this sense.

items.q: Our class won the school football final, ______ everyone because we had lost every practice match.
items.vi: Lớp mình đã thắng trận chung kết bóng đá của trường, điều đó làm mọi người bất ngờ vì bọn mình thua hết các trận giao hữu.
items.explanation: After a comma, which can refer back to the whole previous clause (the fact that we won). That cannot follow a comma in a non-defining clause, what means 'the thing that' and cannot add a comment to a clause, and it would need a new sentence or a conjunction.

items.q: I can't ______ the barking from the neighbours' dogs any longer; it goes on all night.
items.vi: Tôi không thể chịu đựng tiếng sủa của mấy con chó nhà hàng xóm thêm nữa; nó kéo dài suốt đêm.
items.explanation: Put up with means tolerate. Put off is postpone, put out is extinguish, and put away is tidy something into its place.

items.q: The restaurant added a ten per cent service ______ to our bill, so the meal cost more than we expected.
items.vi: Nhà hàng cộng thêm 10% phí phục vụ vào hóa đơn nên bữa ăn đắt hơn chúng tôi tưởng.
items.explanation: A charge is an amount asked for a service, as in service charge; a fare is paid for transport, a price is what goods are sold for, and cost is what you spend overall.

items.q: By the time we reached the market, the fishmonger ______ every last prawn.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi tới chợ thì người bán cá đã bán hết sạch tôm.
items.explanation: The selling finished before another past action (we reached the market), so the past perfect had sold is required.

items.q: There's only ______ milk left in the fridge, so I can't make pancakes for everyone.
items.vi: Trong tủ lạnh chỉ còn một ít sữa nên mình không làm bánh kếp cho cả nhà được.
items.explanation: Milk is uncountable, so it takes a little; a few, few and many go with plural countable nouns.

items.q: You ______ feed the goldfish more than once a day, or it will get sick.
items.vi: Con không được cho cá vàng ăn quá một lần mỗi ngày, nếu không nó sẽ bị bệnh.
items.explanation: Mustn't expresses prohibition — it is forbidden because of the harm. Needn't and don't have to only say something is not necessary, and might not expresses possibility.

items.q: We ______ nearly all our pocket money on snacks at the Mid-Autumn fair.
items.vi: Chúng tôi tiêu gần hết tiền tiêu vặt vào đồ ăn vặt ở hội chợ Trung thu.
items.explanation: You spend money on something; you pay for something, you buy goods rather than money, and things cost money.

items.q: Lan: Your parrot can say a few words, ______? / Nam: Yes, it says 'hello' every morning.
items.vi: Lan: Con vẹt của cậu nói được vài từ, phải không? / Nam: Ừ, sáng nào nó cũng nói 'hello'.
items.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary: can → can't it.

items.q: The vet told us to ______ the puppy a bath every two weeks, not every day.
items.vi: Bác sĩ thú y dặn chúng tôi tắm cho chó con hai tuần một lần, chứ không phải mỗi ngày.
items.explanation: You give an animal (or a child) a bath; you take or have a bath yourself. Make and do do not collocate with a bath.

items.q: If it ______ so heavily, the village wouldn't have called off the boat race.
items.vi: Nếu trời không mưa to như vậy thì làng đã không hủy cuộc đua thuyền.
items.explanation: A past event that did not happen takes the third conditional: if + past perfect (hadn't rained) with would have + past participle in the main clause.

items.q: The soup smelt wonderful; ______, it was far too salty to eat.
items.vi: Món canh thơm tuyệt; tuy nhiên, nó mặn quá không ăn nổi.
items.explanation: The second clause contrasts with the first, so however is needed; therefore shows a result, moreover adds a similar point, and because gives a reason.

items.q: The pet shop gave us a small ______ because the cage had a scratch on one side.
items.vi: Cửa hàng thú cưng giảm giá một chút cho chúng tôi vì cái lồng bị xước một bên.
items.explanation: A discount is an amount taken off the price. A bargain is something bought cheaply, a sale is a period of lower prices, and a bonus is extra money given to a worker.

items.q: Don't forget ______ the hamster's cage before we leave for the festival.
items.vi: Đừng quên dọn lồng chuột hamster trước khi chúng ta đi lễ hội nhé.
items.explanation: Forget to do refers to a task that still needs doing; forget doing means not remember something already done.

items.q: It took Mai several weeks to ______ the loss of her old cat.
items.vi: Mai phải mất mấy tuần mới nguôi ngoai nỗi mất con mèo già của mình.
items.explanation: Get over means recover from an illness or a sad experience. Get by is manage with little money, get along is have a good relationship, and get up is rise from bed.

items.q: Neither the dog nor the cats ______ allowed in the kitchen while Mum is cooking.
items.vi: Cả con chó lẫn mấy con mèo đều không được vào bếp khi mẹ đang nấu ăn.
items.explanation: With neither … nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the cats, so the plural present are is correct.

items.q: You should ______ if the butcher tries to charge more than the price on the sign.
items.vi: Bạn nên giữ vững lập trường nếu người bán thịt cố tính giá cao hơn giá ghi trên bảng.
items.explanation: Stand your ground means refuse to give in. Hold your tongue is stay silent, pull your weight is do your share of the work, and mind your step is be careful where you walk.

items.q: My uncle ______ dogs since he was a little boy, and he still has three.
items.vi: Chú tôi nuôi chó từ hồi còn bé, và giờ chú vẫn nuôi ba con.
items.explanation: Since + a past starting point, for a situation that continues up to now, takes the present perfect: has kept.

items.q: ______ the mooncakes, Mai carried a plate of them next door for the neighbours.
items.vi: Nướng xong bánh trung thu, Mai bưng một đĩa sang nhà hàng xóm.
items.explanation: Having + past participle shows the first action was finished before the second; baking would suggest the two happened at the same time, and baked would make Mai the thing that was baked.

items.q: The two puppies love chasing ______ around the garden all afternoon.
items.vi: Hai chú chó con thích rượt đuổi nhau quanh vườn suốt buổi chiều.
items.explanation: Each other shows the action goes both ways between two subjects; themselves would mean each puppy chases its own self.

items.q: My aunt ______ about 500,000 dong a month by selling homemade fish sauce online.
items.vi: Dì tôi kiếm được khoảng 500.000 đồng một tháng nhờ bán nước mắm nhà làm trên mạng.
items.explanation: You earn money by working or selling; you win a prize, gain experience or weight, and charge a customer a price.

items.q: The whole village ______ part in the lantern parade every autumn.
items.vi: Cả làng đều tham gia rước đèn mỗi mùa thu.
items.explanation: The fixed collocation is take part in (= join an activity); make, do and get do not combine with part in.
